questions.prompt: What does the chapter mean by tails?
choices: Rare outcomes that are much larger than ordinary ones
Results that are always evenly distributed
Events that can be predicted exactly

explanation.gentle: Tails are the rare big outcomes that matter a lot more than normal ones.
explanation.direct: The chapter uses tails to describe outsized events that can dominate the total result.
explanation.competitive: The fat tail is where the giant payoff lives.

questions.prompt: What common myth does the chapter challenge?
choices: That long-run success usually comes from being right almost all the time
That patience can matter in money
That skill matters in any field

explanation.gentle: The chapter says impressive records are often less smooth than people think.
explanation.direct: A few rare outcomes can carry the total instead of steady constant wins doing all the work.
explanation.competitive: The clean-scorecard myth gets broken here.

questions.prompt: Why does survival matter in a tail-driven world?
choices: Because survival keeps you available for the rare outcomes that matter most
Because survival guarantees every outcome will be large
Because survival removes the need for patience

explanation.gentle: You cannot benefit from a rare big win if you are already out of the game.
explanation.direct: Anti-ruin design is part of the upside strategy when tails drive the total.

questions.prompt: What does the chapter say about a weak batting average?
choices: It can still belong to a strong overall record if losses are survivable and a few wins are huge
It always proves the process is broken
It means skill does not matter at all

explanation.gentle: A few big wins can outweigh many ordinary misses.
explanation.direct: The chapter rejects perfectionism in uneven payoff structures.
explanation.competitive: Messy records can still win if the misses do not kill you.

questions.prompt: Why is Lena's product-team decision a Chapter 7 example?
choices: Because one big future win could matter more than the current ordinary middle of the portfolio
Because quiet teams always deserve infinite time
Because all product teams produce equal outcomes

explanation.gentle: The example shows how one rare big result can change the value of the whole record.
explanation.direct: Lena has to judge asymmetry instead of demanding constant proof from every team.
explanation.competitive: She is deciding whether to kill the tail before it lands.

questions.prompt: What does Diego's debate-club postmortem teach?
choices: One championship run can matter more than many ordinary tournaments, so the process must stay alive for rare breakthroughs
Only championships matter in school activities
Average events should be ignored completely

explanation.gentle: The rare big outcome changed the whole year more than the ordinary events did.
explanation.direct: The lesson is to understand the role of tails without turning them into mythology.
explanation.competitive: One spike repriced the whole scoreboard.

questions.prompt: Why can a sound process feel frustrating in this chapter?
choices: Because the biggest contributors may arrive irregularly instead of providing constant proof
Because sound processes always lose money first
Because tails can only happen in financial markets

explanation.gentle: A strong path does not always feel rewarding every week.
explanation.direct: Tail-driven systems can look ordinary for long stretches before the large contribution arrives.
explanation.competitive: The fat-tail world refuses your preferred applause schedule.

questions.prompt: What is the chapter's view of skill?
choices: Skill still matters, but it operates inside an uneven payoff structure
Skill disappears whenever outcomes are uneven
Skill means winning every round

explanation.gentle: The chapter does not deny skill. It puts skill inside a lumpy world.
explanation.direct: Skill helps with process, sizing, survival, and opportunity even when the payoffs are concentrated.
explanation.competitive: Real skill is not constant applause. It is surviving for the oversized round.

questions.prompt: What question becomes more useful than 'How often am I winning?'
choices: Are my losses survivable, and am I still available for the rare opportunities that matter most?
Can I eliminate every miss from the process?
How can I force the world to be more symmetrical?

explanation.gentle: The chapter wants the reader to protect the ability to benefit from future big outcomes.
explanation.direct: Survivability and upside exposure matter more than perfect frequency of wins.

questions.prompt: Why does Tails, You Win lead naturally into Freedom?
choices: Because once a few big outcomes build wealth, the next question is what that wealth is actually for
Because freedom removes the role of uneven outcomes
Because the next chapter rejects all talk of money

explanation.gentle: The chapter shifts from how wealth gets built to what it can create in life.
explanation.direct: Freedom follows because wealth is not only a scorecard once the pile exists.
explanation.competitive: After the tail pays, utility matters more than spectacle.
